attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation does not cover full EF+SAT_U because arbitrary extension formulas can be targets of SAT_U axioms without a proved ExtensionRowRealizer or bounded semantic-row support.
steps: Fix P_gencomp: EF proof syntax plus SAT_U atoms Y_j(x) only for generator rows and declared fanin-b generator-local compositions; no SAT atom may mention an arbitrary extension formula.

Given pi, scan each SAT_U composition axiom. Add a hyperedge S->j from premise rows S to conclusion row j. Let Q_pi be the rows explicitly queried by verifier projections or conclusion-local checks. Define K_pi=cl_{Gamma_pi}(Q_pi).

Construct a spoof completion A^D: outside K_pi use labels induced by a candidate small circuit D_N for H_N^SAT; inside K_pi use the true SAT-row labels. Because K_pi is closed under all semantic hyperedges used by pi, every generator-local SAT axiom seen by pi has the same truth value under A^D as under the true table.

Therefore pi cannot distinguish H_N^SAT from the completed spoof unless it projects a row in K_pi. If pi is accepted and soundly implies LB_epsilon(H_N), then the completed spoof must itself have circuit complexity above N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
But the completed spoof is computed by D_N plus a lookup/row-patching circuit for each charged row, giving C(H_N^SAT)<=S_D+O(|K_pi|N polylog N).

With S_D<=N^{1+epsilon-eta} and |K_pi|<=N^{epsilon-eta}, this contradicts the asserted source lower bound for sufficiently large N. Hence any valid P_gencomp proof must have |K_pi|>=N^{epsilon-o(1)} or avoid the assumptions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It is a valid proof packet for the generator-local composition fragment only. For the main formula-semantic open problem, the missing theorem is that every relevant full EF+SAT_U proof can be reduced to P_gencomp or assigned a target-preserving realizer; the SAT-composition triad is already a falsifier to equality-only extraction.

assumptions: Model: P_gencomp is uniform EF with extension variables allowed only for proof syntax, while SAT_U atoms are restricted to generator-row formulas and named fanin-b row compositions appearing in the generator-local closure.
Uniformity: G_N is computable by circuits of size N^{rho+o(1)} and every row formula has length polylogarithmic in N, so a row truth table over all x has O(N polylog N) hardwirable cost.

Soundness regime: pi proves the lower-bound sentence LB_epsilon(H_N): C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} and the certificate semantics are valid under all row completions satisfying the local SAT composition axioms.
Threshold regime: there is a spoof D_N of size S_D=N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} that agrees with H_N^SAT outside K_pi; if |K_pi|=o(N^epsilon), patching contradicts LB_epsilon.
Non-claim boundary: no assertion is made for full EF+SAT_U with arbitrary introduced formulas unless an extension-to-row realizer maps each semantic SAT atom to bounded generator-row closure.

Use the quotient opener to obtain the label y_[G_N(x,j)] for the parsed formula class; the total query-label cost is N^{q+alpha_ext+o(1)}.
XOR the M_N labels to obtain an approximant D_N(x). By row-parity binding, D_N(x)=H_N^SAT(x) on forced nonresidual rows.
Patch every unforced row and every residual row by equality tests against x; if |B_N|<=N^{f+o(1)} and |R_N|<=N^{r+o(1)}, the patch cost is N^{max(f,r)+1+o(1)}.
Combine generator, opener, and patch circuits to derive C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ext,max(f,r)+1}+o(1)}.
Therefore any proof claiming a larger unrestricted circuit lower bound is invalid within P_wExt under the stated binding and sparsity assumptions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a proof packet for a scoped parser/falsifier theorem, not a proof of P != NP. The remaining validation is to formalize P_wExt syntax and prove row-parity binding for the exact lower-bound sentence rather than assume it as a semantic side condition.

assumptions: Uniform generator regime: M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, formula length L_N=(log N)^d, and G_N has circuits of size N^{rho+o(1)}.

Proof-system regime: pi_N may be hardwired for the negative upper-bound direction, but every semantic identity used by P_wExt is witnessed and parsed into Q_pi; no unwitnessed SAT-extensionality axiom is allowed.
Cover regime: the quotient-label opener has adaptive exponent alpha_ext and is nonuniformly available from pi_N; this is enough for a falsifier upper bound but not a uniform lower-bound consequence.
Binding regime: for each forced row x, all LocSat(Q_pi)-consistent labelings give the true parity xor_j SAT(G_N(x,j)), except for a residual set R_N of size N^{r+o(1)}.
Patch regime: the set B_N of unforced rows has size N^{f+o(1)}, and equality-to-row patches cost O(N) gates per exceptional row.
definitions: source object: H_N^SAT(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) together with a P_wExt proof pi_N of a lower-bound sentence LB_N saying C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
target object: a nonuniform circuit upper-bound falsifier for H_N^SAT with exponent max{rho,q+alpha_ext,max(f,r)+1}.
controlled interface: a parser maps SAT occurrences in pi_N to an equality/equisatisfiability quotient Q_pi, plus a label-opener for quotient classes with adaptive cover exponent alpha_ext.

target-preserving condition: row-parity binding holds on all forced rows and the remaining semantic residual and unforced rows have exponents r and f, so the constructed approximant agrees with the real SAT parity off a patchable sparse set.

P_wExt is EF plus SAT atoms and witnessed extensionality rules; every formula identity or equisatisfiability inference carries a syntactic witness such as definitional extension, variable renaming, or an EF-checkable Tseitin map.
ForcedRows(Q_pi) are rows whose XOR of quotient labels is constant over all locally SAT-consistent assignments admitted by the parsed proof transcript.

equations.label: carrier_definition
equations.latex: H_N^{SAT}(x)=\bigoplus_{j\le M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)),\quad M_N\le N^{q+o(1)},\quad |G_N|\le N^{\rho+o(1)}
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source carrier is the beta-zero SAT-XOR family with polylogarithmic SAT instances and explicitly bounded generator overhead.

equations.label: adaptive_extensional_cover
equations.valid_when: Valid when witnessed formula identities contract to quotient-openers with transcript, summary, and local-opening exponents tau, a_l+mu_l, and omega_l.

equations.label: forced_rows_definition
equations.latex: ForcedRows(Q_\pi)=\{x:\bigoplus_{j\le M_N} y_{[G_N(x,j)]}\text{ is constant over }LocSat(Q_\pi)\}
equations.valid_when: Valid when every SAT occurrence is assigned to a parsed quotient class and LocSat contains exactly the locally admissible quotient labelings.

equations.label: patch_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after row-parity binding is established on forced rows and all unforced or residual rows are patched by explicit equality tests.

equations.label: certificate_falsifier_threshold
equations.latex: 1+\epsilon>\max\{\rho,q+\alpha_{ext},\max(f,r)+1\}\Rightarrow \pi_N\text{ is not a valid certificate of }C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+\epsilon-o(1)}
equations.valid_when: Requires the lower-bound sentence to target unrestricted nonuniform circuits and the parsed proof transcript to satisfy the witnessed-extensionality cover assumptions.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find one accepted P_wExt proof using only witnessed extensionality where the quotient parser has alpha_ext below threshold, row-parity binding holds, sparse residual bounds hold, yet no circuit satisfying the patch upper bound can be built.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-specific finite falsifier theorem for witnessed formula-semantic proof systems; it supports the draft extraction fork without claiming P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the beta-zero SAT-XOR carrier, any P_wExt proof whose formula-identity and equisatisfiability uses are witnessed by a low-adaptive-cover quotient yields the same patch upper bound as the occurrence-local parser. Thus such a proof cannot validly certify C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} when the cap exponent is below 1+epsilon.

assumptions: Extensionality calls are not accompanied by definitional, resolution, EF, or Tseitin certificates whose size and cover exponent are bounded.
The parser is required to be proof-local: it may inspect pi_N but may not solve arbitrary semantic equivalence of polylogarithmic SAT formulas by importing hidden advice.
The no-go is a route-level obstruction for this extraction method, not a lower bound against all possible semantic proof systems.
definitions: source object is a P_uExt proof pi_N extending EF+SAT atoms by an axiom Ext(F,F') that is sound whenever F and F' are equisatisfiable.
target object is either a low-cover quotient transcript Q_pi or a named nonrelativizing semantic principle blocking such a transcript.
controlled interface is the attempted map from each Ext(F,F') call to a finite equality graph or local transformation witness.
observable is whether the parser can assign occurrence labels while preserving all row parities under private-row spoofing.

equations.label: unwitnessed_extensionality_rule
equations.valid_when: Valid when the proof system explicitly includes a sound but unparsed semantic equisatisfiability rule for SAT formulas.

equations.label: parser_gap
equations.valid_when: Valid when no syntactic witness is supplied and the extraction algorithm is restricted to proof-local data rather than semantic advice.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Produce a uniform proof-local parser that converts every sound unwitnessed Ext step into a low-cover quotient while preserving row parities and without deciding hidden SAT equivalence by advice.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: No-go boundary for the parser theorem; names the exact nonrelativizing SAT-semantic principle that escapes the low-cover falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Unwitnessed SAT-extensionality is the minimal semantic escape from the occurrence/quotient parser: if a proof step may assert SAT(F)<->SAT(F') from semantic equisatisfiability without a checkable witness, then the low-cover parser need not exist, and the previous falsifier theorem is invalid outside P_wExt.

assumptions: The negative direction permits hardwiring a fixed accepted certificate, so selector advice is irrelevant for obtaining an upper-bound falsifier.
The carrier is intended to certify MCSP no-side hardness at threshold 2^{theta m-o(m)} for row truth tables of length 2^m.
The label opener is valid for all queried SAT instances in the beta-zero transcript, not only for a sampled or aggregate subset.
definitions: source object is an MCSP/MKtP label certificate family supplying truth labels or row-hardness witnesses for SAT-XOR proof transcripts.
target object is the row function x -> xor_j label(G_N(x,j)) used to approximate H_N^SAT.
controlled interface is the adaptive label opener with transcript exponent tau, summary exponents a_l+mu_l, and opening exponents omega_l.
observable is whether the carrier supplies advice-free row-hardness or merely a nonuniformly selectable hard row.

equations.label: mcsp_adaptive_cover_cap
equations.valid_when: Valid when the accepted MCSP or MKtP carrier exposes row bits through the stated adaptive cover without additional unparsed semantic hardness.

equations.label: beta_zero_label_cap
equations.valid_when: Applies when MCSP-carrier labels replace SAT labels on all nonresidual beta-zero queries and residual rows are explicitly patched.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit an MCSP/MKtP label carrier with alpha_ad<theta that nevertheless prevents the hardwired opener circuit from computing the certified row labels.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Carrier-transfer audit supporting the formula-semantic packet; it is a falsifier for low-cover meta-complexity labels.
candidate_lemmas.statement: An MCSP/MKtP certificate carrier used as the label source for P_wExt is harmless only if its label opener has adaptive cover at least the claimed hardness threshold; if alpha_ad<theta, hardwiring the carrier gives a subthreshold row circuit and falsifies the no-side source claim.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if P_wExt cannot be specified without smuggling in unwitnessed semantic Ext, or if row-parity binding cannot be derived from the lower-bound sentence.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after a formal P_wExt definition, a checked parser pi -> Q_pi, a proved row-parity binding lemma, and an inference-quality packet with prior-art boundary.

dependency_updates.description: Define EF+SAT_U with witnessed extensionality rules, accepted witness types, and quotient-cover accounting.
Prove that the lower-bound sentence plus P_wExt soundness forces true SAT parity on ForcedRows(Q_pi), not merely local consistency.
Full systems with unparsed SAT-extensionality remain outside the low-cover falsifier and must be classified as genuinely nonrelativizing semantic routes.
Any MCSP/MKtP label source proposed for the proof transcript must report alpha_ad and survive the subthreshold opener test.
Compare the scoped theorem against known natural-proofs, MCSP, EF, and SAT-oracle proof-complexity results without promoting it to a global lower-bound claim.

falsifiers: A single unwitnessed SAT-extensionality rule is a falsifier for the low-cover parser because the occurrence quotient may require semantic equivalence information absent from the proof transcript.
If alpha_ext<1+epsilon-q and f,r<epsilon, the constructed circuit upper bound falsifies any claimed N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} lower-bound certificate in P_wExt.
If row-parity binding fails, a private-label spoof on a nonforced row gives a countermodel to the proof-to-query extraction even when ordinary local soundness holds.
If an MCSP/MKtP carrier has adaptive cover alpha_ad below its claimed threshold theta, the carrier supplies its own row circuit and is not a valid no-side source.

If the proof uses nonuniform hard-row selection to choose labels but gives no advice-free searchable certificate, it may show aggregate hardness only and cannot transfer to a uniform language lower bound.
